summary: Read-only: audit all 11 optimizers L3-TC staged paths vs their canonical algorithm (header + per-op kernel + Python) for SG11-class drift (re-inlined reductions with wrong operand/term/order); cost-calibrated models; adversarially verify each candidate drift
logs: Audited 11 optimizers; 11 candidate divergences flagged; verifying each (opus, refute-by-default).

confirmed_drifts.divergence: HISTORICAL (already remediated in the main tree, not an active drift). The L3-TC staged gate at opt_stages_precompute.cuh re-inlined the canonical cosine reduction with the WRONG 2nd operand: cos(grad, MU) instead of the canonical cos(grad, MOMENTUM). The current main-tree code is now FAITHFUL: sg11_precompute_mu_and_gate_for_tensor (opt_stages_precompute.cuh:541-561) declares local num/den_g/den_m, then per element CALLS algo::sg11_sweep_a_step(mu_blob, grad, sharpness, momentum, mu_val, gi, num, den_g, den_m) (line 547-548) — the single source that accumulates num+=g*m, den_g+=g*g, den_m+=m*m with m=momentum — and finalizes via canonical algo::sg11_finalize_gate(num, den_g, den_m, gate_temp) (line 561). The decoder call site (fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:1458-1460) passes st.exp_avg (the START-OF-STEP momentum, written only later by sg11_sweep_b_step) as the momentum operand. Term-for-term matches canonical supergrok11.h.
confirmed_drifts.severity: none-now (remediated); was HIGH — a wrong 2nd cosine operand corrupts the per-tensor gate=sigmoid(gate_temp*cos), which scales the entire (1-gate)*alpha*mu smart-grad term every step
confirmed_drifts.fix_sketch: Already applied: staged path CALLS sg11_sweep_a_step + sg11_finalize_gate instead of re-inlining; momentum operand = st.exp_avg (start-of-step). No further SG11 code change needed. VERIFY before re-gating: (1) de-mirror the fp64 oracle so it does NOT recompute the kernel formula; (2) re-run a multi-step WARM-UP gate (>=3-5 steps, non-trivial exp_avg) on 3 seeds so the step-1 coincidence cannot fake-green it.
confirmed_drifts.gate_note: GATE WAS BLIND for TWO compounding reasons, both must close before re-gating: (1) the fp64 oracle MIRRORED the kernel — it computed cos(grad,mu) too, so kernel==oracle and parity passed CO-WRONG; (2) a step-1 COINCIDENCE: at step 1 the start-of-step momentum exp_avg is still ~0 (or grad-seeded), so cos(grad,momentum) degenerates and both operands give near-identical gates at t=1, defeating a single-step fp64 gate. Re-gate with a CORRECTED, INDEPENDENT fp64 oracle (recompute cos(grad,momentum) from first principles, NOT by re-running the kernel expression) AND a multi-step warm-up so the operand divergence is numerically large. Anchor to 3 seeds per the patch protocol.

synth.guard_gap: scripts/check_math_single_source.py was EXTENDED for the SG11 case (1c, lines 217-243 + 454-470: _COSINE_REINLINE_PATTERNS now scans opt_stages_precompute.cuh for `den_m += x*x` / `den_g += x*x` and asserts the #include of supergrok11.h), which closes the exact SG11 hole. THREE residual gaps remain against the broader class: (A) NARROW-TOKEN — the cosine patterns only match the literal accumulator names `den_m`/`den_g`; a staged reduction re-inlining the same cos(a,b) with different names (e.g. num/dg/dm, or SG2's CSA scores) is NOT caught. Make it structural (any `<id> += <expr>*<expr>` inside a reduction loop in a staged precompute header) or lift the operand risk into the oracle, see (D). (B) SCOPE — the GENERAL Adam-reinline scan (_consumer_headers(), lines 246-255, feeding scan_reinlined_math) still scans ONLY opt_components.cuh, NOT opt_stages_precompute.cuh or opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh. Add both staged headers to _consumer_headers() so a re-inlined moment-update / `(m/bc1)/(sqrtf(v/bc2)+eps)` apply re-typed in a STAGE (and the GrokAdamW/NeuralGrok EMA+amplification re-inlines in the tail) is flagged. (C) NO CALL-ARGUMENT CHECK — even with #include + apply-symbol asserted, the guard cannot see that a CALL passes the RIGHT operand: sg11_sweep_a_step(...,momentum,...) vs sg11_sweep_a_step(...,mu,...) both satisfy `calls the canonical fn` and both PASS. This is the true SG11 root cause and is fundamentally SEMANTIC, not structural. (D) RECOMMENDED CLOSURE — make the fp64 --self-test numeric oracle the real tooth: register every staged PRECOMPUTE (not just the apply tail) with an INDEPENDENT reference (never derived by re-running the kernel expression), run it WARMED-UP (multi-step, non-trivial momentum/EMA state) so step-1 coincidences cannot fake-green, and have the prove-it-triggers test perturb a staged operand (swap momentum->mu) to confirm the oracle flags it. Also add opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh to BOTH the cosine-consumer and Adam-reinline consumer lists (its CSA softmax + GRU + grokfast-EMA math is currently scanned by nothing).
synth.notes:
SCOPE/STATE: Audited the MAIN working tree /workspace/SuperGrok1.5 (NOT the .claude/worktrees/* copies — sibling-agent owned). My independent line-by-line read CONFIRMS no optimizer currently carries an ACTIVE SG11-class wrong-operand drift; all 11 audit faithful:true holds. The one confirmed_drift is the SG11 case as a REMEDIATED/forward record — its gate stays blind until the oracle is de-mirrored + warmed up (the load-bearing follow-up for the ratchet). Per-op `<opt>_sm90.cuh` kernels referenced by SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md were REMOVED in Task #10 (production is pure L3-TC); the surviving CUDA consumers are opt_components.cuh + the staged headers, all deriving from csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h.

WHY THE non-zero n_div ENTRIES ARE CLEAN (re-expressions, not divergences):
- supergrok2 (n_div=2): staged S5 apply (opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh:1007) CALLS canonical sg2_apply_step (supergrok2.h:395 — GRU mu_new, grokfast slow_new, smart_grad=g+alpha*mu_new+lamb_eff*slow_new, Adam tail) term-for-term. CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU/segmented-sort meta-net is NEW device code with no per-element canonical equivalent (like Muon's matmuls). Guard exempts SG2 as a WARN (separate launch_csa_hca path).
- supergrok15 (n_div=2): sg15_precompute_mu_for_tensor (opt_stages_precompute.cuh:594-611) RE-INLINES mu_blob[gi]=rescale*sg15_phi_forward(...) rather than calling sg15_sweep_a_step. BENIGN: mu value identical; the only dropped term (sharp_local+=grad*grad) feeds the NEXT step's sharpness host-side, is NOT consumed by this step's apply (reads mu + host gate st.gate), documented at lines 578-583. STRUCTURALLY the same re-inline shape as SG11's danger but operand (rescale*phi) is CORRECT — keep on watch-list.
- neuralgrok (n_div=2): tail (opt_components.cuh:483-495) calls canonical neuralgrok_psi_forward + neuralgrok_apply_step; on-device psi_b2 read + clip_coef scale are documented ABI/clip extensions, not math changes.
- looksam (n_div=2): NO staged precompute by design (model-coupled sam_dir from 2nd backward); tail calls canonical looksam_apply_step. Divergences = documented model-stage/ABI contract.
- muon (n_div=3): NS combine calls canonical muon_ns_combine_step (line 429); buf=momentum*buf+grad matches muon.h:43; matmuls + Frobenius norm are NEW device code (live path uses torch::mm/cuBLAS). Constants 3.4445/-4.7750/2.0315 + 1e-7 eps match. inv_norm=1/(sqrtf(s)+1e-7) is hand-typed (muon_norm_reduce_phaseB) only because muon.h exposes no such helper (normalize_step takes inv_norm as an arg) — matches bindings.cpp:962-963.

GrokAdamW WATCH-ITEM (currently CORRECT, flagged only for guard coverage): apply tail (opt_components.cuh:450-466) RE-INLINES the EMA filter ema_new=alpha*ema+(1-alpha)*gc + amplification g_amp=gc+lamb*ema_new (then calls canonical grokadamw_adam_tail for the Adam apply). This re-inline is FORCED (must inject device-computed global-clip coef gc + per-tensor beta1, which grokadamw_step cannot express) and is documented bit-faithful vs grokadamw.h:48-52, but it is the SAME re-inline class as SG11 and the EMA/amplification portion is UNGUARDED — strongest concrete case for guard_gap (B)+(D).

GUARD RUN: python3 scripts/check_math_single_source.py exits 0 (OK) with only the expected SG2-separate-path WARN. Cosine re-inline scan finds no hits (the only den_m/den_g += are inside the CALLED canonical sg11_sweep_a_step; the local num/den_g/den_m=0 decls + block_reduce_sum_f32 finalizers correctly do not match)."
